name: BOOLEAN_TRUE_FALSE_NULL
description: Boolean literal acceptance and rendering
stdin: SELECT true, false, NULL::boolean;

name: BOOLEAN_CAST_FROM_TEXT
description: Boolean cast from text accepts 'yes', 'no', '1', '0', 'true', 'false'
stdin: SELECT 'yes'::bool, 'no'::bool, '1'::bool, '0'::bool, 't'::bool, 'f'::bool;

name: BOOLEAN_LOGIC_THREE_VALUED
description: Three-valued boolean logic returns NULL on either-NULL operand
stdin: SELECT true AND NULL, false OR NULL, NULL = NULL, NULL IS NULL;

name: DECIMAL_BASIC_ARITH
description: DECIMAL(10,2) preserves exact decimal arithmetic
stdin: SELECT 0.1::numeric + 0.2::numeric, (1.5::numeric * 3)::numeric(10,2);

name: DECIMAL_NO_LOSS_VS_REAL
description: DECIMAL preserves precision where REAL would lose
stdin: SELECT 0.1::numeric + 0.2::numeric = 0.3::numeric, 0.1::real + 0.2::real = 0.3::real;

name: DECIMAL_DIVISION
description: NUMERIC division yields exact result
stdin: SELECT 10::numeric / 3::numeric;

name: UUID_LITERAL_AND_TYPEOF
description: UUID literal cast and self-comparison

name: UUID_GEN_RANDOM_DETERMINISM
description: gen_random_uuid produces v4 UUIDs (length stable; value nondeterministic — verify shape only)
stdin: SELECT length(gen_random_uuid()::text) = 36;

name: TIMESTAMPTZ_AT_UTC
description: TIMESTAMPTZ with explicit timezone
stdin: SELECT '2025-01-15 12:00:00+00'::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC';

name: TIMESTAMP_DIFF_INTERVAL
description: Subtracting two timestamps yields INTERVAL
stdin: SELECT '2025-01-02'::timestamp - '2025-01-01'::timestamp;

name: INTERVAL_ADD_TO_DATE
description: INTERVAL arithmetic on DATE
stdin: SELECT '2025-01-01'::date + INTERVAL '5 days';

name: DATE_TRUNC_MONTH
description: date_trunc('month', ...) zeros out sub-month fields
stdin: SELECT date_trunc('month', '2025-04-17 13:25:00'::timestamp);

name: ARRAY_LITERAL_AND_LENGTH
description: Native array literal + array_length
stdin: SELECT ARRAY[10,20,30], array_length(ARRAY[10,20,30], 1);

name: ARRAY_CONTAINS_OPERATOR
description: @> array containment
stdin: SELECT ARRAY[1,2,3] @> ARRAY[2,3], ARRAY[1,2] @> ARRAY[3];

name: ARRAY_OVERLAP_OPERATOR
description: && array overlap
stdin: SELECT ARRAY[1,2,3] && ARRAY[3,4,5], ARRAY[1,2] && ARRAY[10,11];

name: ARRAY_INDEX_ONE_BASED
description: Postgres arrays are 1-indexed by default
stdin: SELECT (ARRAY['a','b','c'])[1], (ARRAY['a','b','c'])[3];

name: ARRAY_AGG_OF_INTS
description: array_agg aggregate produces an ARRAY value
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3)) SELECT array_agg(x ORDER BY x DESC) FROM v;

name: UNNEST_ARRAY_TO_ROWS
description: UNNEST expands an ARRAY into rows
stdin: SELECT * FROM unnest(ARRAY[10,20,30]) ORDER BY 1;

name: TEXT_ARRAY_CONCAT
description: TEXT[] || TEXT[] concatenates
stdin: SELECT ARRAY['a','b'] || ARRAY['c','d'];

name: ENUM_CREATE_AND_USE
description: CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM defines a constrained value set
setup_stdin: DROP TYPE IF EXISTS mood CASCADE; CREATE TYPE mood AS ENUM ('happy','sad','meh');
stdin: SELECT 'happy'::mood, 'sad'::mood < 'happy'::mood;

name: ENUM_REJECTS_BAD_VALUE
description: ENUM cast rejects values outside the declared set
setup_stdin: DROP TYPE IF EXISTS color CASCADE; CREATE TYPE color AS ENUM ('red','green','blue');
stdin: SELECT 'purple'::color;

name: DOMAIN_TYPE_BASIC
description: CREATE DOMAIN defines a reusable constrained type
setup_stdin: DROP DOMAIN IF EXISTS positive_int CASCADE; CREATE DOMAIN positive_int AS INTEGER CHECK (VALUE > 0);
stdin: SELECT 5::positive_int;

name: DOMAIN_REJECTS_NEG
description: DOMAIN check rejects bad value at cast
setup_stdin: DROP DOMAIN IF EXISTS positive_int2 CASCADE; CREATE DOMAIN positive_int2 AS INTEGER CHECK (VALUE > 0);
stdin: SELECT (-5)::positive_int2;

name: JSONB_BASIC_ROUNDTRIP
description: JSONB parses + emits in canonical form
stdin: SELECT '{"b":1,"a":2}'::jsonb;

name: JSONB_OBJECT_KEYS
description: jsonb_object_keys enumerates keys
stdin: SELECT * FROM jsonb_object_keys('{"a":1,"b":2}'::jsonb) ORDER BY 1;

name: RANGE_INT4RANGE_CONTAINS
description: int4range containment via @>
stdin: SELECT int4range(1,10) @> 5, int4range(1,10) @> 10;

name: RANGE_OVERLAP
description: Range && overlap operator
stdin: SELECT int4range(1,5) && int4range(3,9);

name: MONEY_RENDER
description: MONEY type renders with the active lc_monetary
stdin: SELECT 123.45::money;

name: BYTEA_HEX_LITERAL
description: BYTEA hex literal '\x...' parses and renders
stdin: SELECT '\x01ab'::bytea, length('\x01ab'::bytea);

name: POINT_GEOMETRY
description: POINT literal and distance operator
stdin: SELECT point(0,0) <-> point(3,4);

name: ILIKE_BASIC_MIXED_CASE
description: ILIKE matches case-insensitively for ASCII letters
stdin: SELECT 'ABC' ILIKE 'abc', 'ABC' ILIKE 'AbC', 'ABC' ILIKE 'xyz';

name: ILIKE_PERCENT_WILDCARD
description: ILIKE with % wildcard matches any sequence regardless of case
stdin: SELECT 'Hello World' ILIKE '%world%', 'Hello World' ILIKE 'hello%', 'Hello World' ILIKE '%xyz%';

name: ILIKE_UNDERSCORE_WILDCARD
description: ILIKE underscore matches exactly one character in any case
stdin: SELECT 'ABC' ILIKE 'a_c', 'ABCDE' ILIKE 'a_c', 'A1C' ILIKE 'A_C';

name: ILIKE_ESCAPE_CLAUSE
description: ILIKE with explicit ESCAPE clause to match a literal percent
stdin: SELECT '50%' ILIKE '50!%' ESCAPE '!', 'A%B' ILIKE 'a!%b' ESCAPE '!', '50' ILIKE '50!%' ESCAPE '!';

name: NOT_ILIKE_BASIC
description: NOT ILIKE returns the boolean negation of ILIKE
stdin: SELECT 'ABC' NOT ILIKE 'abc', 'XYZ' NOT ILIKE 'abc', NULL NOT ILIKE 'x';

name: ILIKE_WITH_NULL
description: ILIKE returns NULL when either operand is NULL (SQL three-valued logic)
stdin: SELECT NULL ILIKE 'abc', 'abc' ILIKE NULL, NULL ILIKE NULL;

name: ILIKE_ANCHORED_FULL_MATCH
description: ILIKE is anchored at both ends — partial substring needs explicit %
stdin: SELECT 'abcdef' ILIKE 'abc', 'abcdef' ILIKE 'abc%', 'abcdef' ILIKE '%abc';

name: CITEXT_CREATE_EXTENSION
description: CREATE EXTENSION citext succeeds (extension is available on this cluster)
setup_stdin: DROP EXTENSION IF EXISTS citext; CREATE EXTENSION citext;
stdin: SELECT 'ABC'::citext = 'abc'::citext;

name: CITEXT_EQ_CASE_INSENSITIVE
description: citext equality is case-insensitive even when one side is a text literal coerced
setup_stdin: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citext;
stdin: SELECT 'Hello'::citext = 'HELLO', 'Hello'::citext = 'hello', 'Hello'::citext <> 'world';

name: CITEXT_ORDER_BY
description: citext ORDER BY ignores case in comparisons
setup_stdin: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citext;
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES ('banana'::citext),('Apple'::citext),('CHERRY'::citext)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x;

name: COLLATE_C_VS_ICU_ASCII
description: COLLATE "C" orders uppercase before lowercase; ICU collates dictionary-style
stdin: SELECT ('a' < 'B' COLLATE "C")::text || '|' || ('a' < 'B' COLLATE "en-x-icu")::text;

name: COLLATE_C_SORT_ORDER
description: ORDER BY ... COLLATE "C" yields ASCII byte order (uppercase first)
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES ('apple'),('Banana'),('Apple'),('banana')) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x COLLATE "C";

name: COLLATE_ICU_LANGUAGE_SORT
description: ORDER BY ... COLLATE "en-x-icu" yields dictionary-style case-insensitive primary sort
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES ('apple'),('Banana'),('Apple'),('banana')) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x COLLATE "en-x-icu", x COLLATE "C";

name: COLLATE_UND_X_ICU_AVAILABLE
description: The root "und-x-icu" ICU collation is available and usable in expressions
stdin: SELECT 'a' < 'B' COLLATE "und-x-icu";

name: COLLATE_CUSTOM_CI_NONDETERMINISTIC
description: Create nondeterministic ICU collation (case-insensitive) and use it in equality
setup_stdin: DROP COLLATION IF EXISTS beyond_ci CASCADE; CREATE COLLATION beyond_ci (provider = icu, locale = 'und-u-ks-level2', deterministic = false);
stdin: SELECT 'ABC' = 'abc' COLLATE beyond_ci, 'ABC' = 'xyz' COLLATE beyond_ci;

name: COLLATE_ACCENT_INSENSITIVE
description: Nondeterministic ICU collation with level=1 treats accents as equal
setup_stdin: DROP COLLATION IF EXISTS beyond_ai CASCADE; CREATE COLLATION beyond_ai (provider = icu, locale = 'und-u-ks-level1', deterministic = false);
stdin: SELECT 'cafe' = 'café' COLLATE beyond_ai, 'Cafe' = 'CAFÉ' COLLATE beyond_ai;

name: LOWER_MULTIBYTE_UNICODE
description: lower() lowercases multibyte characters per the database locale
stdin: SELECT lower('ÉCOLE'), lower('ÄÖÜ');

name: UPPER_GREEK_SIGMA
description: upper() on Greek lowercase produces uppercase Greek; sigma stays canonical
stdin: SELECT upper('αβγ'), upper('σς');

name: UPPER_GERMAN_ESZETT
description: upper() on German ß depends on locale; PG default yields 'SS'
stdin: SELECT upper('straße');

name: ORDER_BY_LOWER_TRICK_NOCASE
description: Case-insensitive ORDER BY via lower() trick is portable across engines
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES ('Banana'),('apple'),('CHERRY')) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY lower(x);

name: REGEX_CASE_SENSITIVE_TILDE
description: The ~ operator is case-sensitive POSIX regex match
stdin: SELECT 'Hello' ~ 'ello', 'Hello' ~ 'ELLO', 'Hello' ~ '^H';

name: REGEX_CASE_INSENSITIVE_TILDESTAR
description: The ~* operator is case-insensitive POSIX regex match
stdin: SELECT 'Hello' ~* 'ello', 'Hello' ~* 'ELLO', 'Hello' !~* 'XYZ';

name: REGEX_NEGATED_NOT_TILDE
description: The !~ and !~* operators negate regex match
stdin: SELECT 'Hello' !~ 'XYZ', 'Hello' !~* 'ELLO', 'Hello' !~ '^H';

name: SIMILAR_TO_BASIC
description: SIMILAR TO accepts SQL-standard regex with %, _, and alternation
stdin: SELECT 'abc' SIMILAR TO 'a%', 'abc' SIMILAR TO '(a|b)bc', 'abc' SIMILAR TO 'a_c';

name: SIMILAR_TO_CHARACTER_CLASS
description: SIMILAR TO supports POSIX bracket character classes
stdin: SELECT 'abc1' SIMILAR TO '[a-z]+[0-9]+', 'ABC' SIMILAR TO '[a-z]+', 'ABC' SIMILAR TO '[A-Z]+';

name: POSITION_MULTIBYTE
description: position() is measured in characters even when input has multibyte glyphs
stdin: SELECT position('é' IN 'café'), position('e' IN 'école');

name: LENGTH_VS_OCTET_LENGTH_MULTIBYTE
description: length() counts characters; octet_length() counts bytes; multibyte differs
stdin: SELECT length('café'), octet_length('café'), length('αβγ'), octet_length('αβγ');

name: ILIKE_NON_ASCII_DOES_NOT_FOLD
description: ILIKE folds ASCII case but locale-dependent for non-ASCII; PG default folds via lower
stdin: SELECT 'CAFÉ' ILIKE 'café', 'CAFÉ' ILIKE 'cafe';

name: LIKE_VS_ILIKE_ASCII
description: LIKE is case-sensitive, ILIKE is case-insensitive on the same pattern
stdin: SELECT 'AbCdEf' LIKE '%cd%', 'AbCdEf' ILIKE '%cd%', 'AbCdEf' LIKE '%CD%';

name: ORDER_BY_COLLATE_NULLS_LAST
description: ORDER BY combining COLLATE with NULLS LAST orders by ICU rules then puts NULL last
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES ('banana'),('Apple'),(NULL),('cherry')) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x COLLATE "en-x-icu" NULLS LAST;

name: MERGE_UPDATE_AND_INSERT
description: MERGE INTO with WHEN MATCHED UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED INSERT branches
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_t CASCADE;DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_s CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_merge_t (id int primary key, v text);CREATE TABLE bp_merge_s (id int, v text);INSERT INTO bp_merge_t VALUES (1, 'a');INSERT INTO bp_merge_s VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B');
stdin:
MERGE INTO bp_merge_t t USING bp_merge_s s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v = s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, v) VALUES (s.id, s.v);
SELECT * FROM bp_merge_t ORDER BY id;

name: MERGE_MATCHED_DELETE
description: MERGE WHEN MATCHED DELETE removes matched target rows
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_d_t CASCADE;DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_d_s CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_merge_d_t (id int primary key, v int);CREATE TABLE bp_merge_d_s (id int);INSERT INTO bp_merge_d_t VALUES (1,10),(2,20),(3,30);INSERT INTO bp_merge_d_s VALUES (2);
stdin:
MERGE INTO bp_merge_d_t t USING bp_merge_d_s s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE;
SELECT * FROM bp_merge_d_t ORDER BY id;

name: MERGE_CONDITIONAL_BRANCHES
description: MERGE with multiple WHEN MATCHED branches gated by AND predicates
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_c_t CASCADE;DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_c_s CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_merge_c_t (id int primary key, v int);CREATE TABLE bp_merge_c_s (id int, v int, op text);INSERT INTO bp_merge_c_t VALUES (1,100),(2,200),(3,300);INSERT INTO bp_merge_c_s VALUES (1, NULL, 'del'),(2, 999, 'upd'),(4, 400, 'ins');
stdin:
MERGE INTO bp_merge_c_t t USING bp_merge_c_s s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'del' THEN DELETE WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'upd' THEN UPDATE SET v = s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED AND s.op = 'ins' THEN INSERT (id, v) VALUES (s.id, s.v);
SELECT * FROM bp_merge_c_t ORDER BY id;

name: MERGE_NOT_MATCHED_BY_SOURCE_PG17
description: MERGE ... WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE is PG17+; PG16 should error
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_nms_t CASCADE;DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_merge_nms_s CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_merge_nms_t (id int primary key);CREATE TABLE bp_merge_nms_s (id int);INSERT INTO bp_merge_nms_t VALUES (1),(2);INSERT INTO bp_merge_nms_s VALUES (1);
stdin: MERGE INTO bp_merge_nms_t t USING bp_merge_nms_s s ON t.id = s.id WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;
notes: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE landed in PG17; PG16 raises a syntax error.

name: CROSS_JOIN_LATERAL_SCALAR
description: CROSS JOIN LATERAL evaluates the right side per outer row
stdin: SELECT t.x, l.y FROM (VALUES (1),(2),(3)) AS t(x) CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT t.x * 10 AS y) AS l ORDER BY t.x;

name: LEFT_JOIN_LATERAL_OPTIONAL
description: LEFT JOIN LATERAL preserves outer rows when right side returns zero rows
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_lat_a CASCADE;DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_lat_b CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_lat_a (id int);CREATE TABLE bp_lat_b (a_id int, v int);INSERT INTO bp_lat_a VALUES (1),(2),(3);INSERT INTO bp_lat_b VALUES (1,10),(1,20);
stdin: SELECT a.id, l.v FROM bp_lat_a a LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT v FROM bp_lat_b WHERE bp_lat_b.a_id = a.id ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 1) l ON TRUE ORDER BY a.id;

name: LATERAL_WITH_SET_RETURNING_FUNCTION
description: LATERAL with generate_series expands each outer row into N rows
stdin: SELECT t.x, g FROM (VALUES (1),(2)) AS t(x) CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1, t.x) AS g ORDER BY t.x, g;

name: DMCTE_INSERT_RETURNING
description: WITH x AS (INSERT ... RETURNING *) feeds inserted rows into outer SELECT
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_dmcte_i CASCADE; CREATE TABLE bp_dmcte_i (id int, v text);
stdin: WITH ins AS (INSERT INTO bp_dmcte_i VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b') RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM ins ORDER BY id;

name: DMCTE_UPDATE_RETURNING
description: WITH x AS (UPDATE ... RETURNING *) feeds updated rows into outer SELECT
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_dmcte_u CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_dmcte_u (id int, n int);INSERT INTO bp_dmcte_u VALUES (1,10),(2,20);
stdin: WITH upd AS (UPDATE bp_dmcte_u SET n = n * 2 RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM upd ORDER BY id;

name: DMCTE_DELETE_RETURNING_COUNT
description: WITH x AS (DELETE ... RETURNING *) lets outer SELECT count deleted rows
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_dmcte_d CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_dmcte_d (id int);INSERT INTO bp_dmcte_d VALUES (1),(2),(3);
stdin: WITH del AS (DELETE FROM bp_dmcte_d WHERE id > 1 RETURNING *) SELECT count(*) FROM del;

name: DISTINCT_ON_FIRST_PER_GROUP
description: DISTINCT ON (g) keeps first row per group per ORDER BY
stdin: WITH v(g,x) AS (VALUES (1,'a'),(1,'b'),(1,'c'),(2,'p'),(2,'q')) SELECT DISTINCT ON (g) g,x FROM v ORDER BY g, x DESC;

name: DISTINCT_ON_REQUIRES_ORDER_BY
description: DISTINCT ON expressions must be the leftmost ORDER BY terms; mismatch errors
stdin: WITH v(g,x) AS (VALUES (1,'a'),(1,'b')) SELECT DISTINCT ON (g) g,x FROM v ORDER BY x;

name: DISTINCT_ON_MULTIPLE_COLS
description: DISTINCT ON with multiple expressions picks first row per (col1,col2) bucket
stdin: WITH v(g1,g2,x) AS (VALUES (1,'x',1),(1,'x',2),(1,'y',3),(2,'x',4)) SELECT DISTINCT ON (g1,g2) g1,g2,x FROM v ORDER BY g1,g2,x DESC;

name: DEFAULT_IN_VALUES
description: DEFAULT keyword inside VALUES uses the column default expression
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_default_v CASCADE; CREATE TABLE bp_default_v (id int DEFAULT 99, v text);
stdin:
INSERT INTO bp_default_v VALUES (DEFAULT, 'x'), (5, 'y');
SELECT * FROM bp_default_v ORDER BY v;

name: VALUES_STANDALONE_SOURCE
description: VALUES can be a top-level statement returning multi-row literal

name: VALUES_IN_JOIN
description: VALUES as a derived table joined via FROM clause
stdin: SELECT u.id, u.name FROM (VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b'),(3,'c')) AS u(id,name) ORDER BY id;

name: SELECT_INTO_NEW_TABLE
description: SELECT INTO creates a new table from a query's result set
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_selinto CASCADE;
stdin:
SELECT 1 AS x, 'y'::text AS y INTO bp_selinto;
SELECT * FROM bp_selinto;

name: WINDOW_NAMED_REUSE
description: WINDOW clause defines a named window reused by multiple OVER(w) calls
stdin: WITH v(g,x) AS (VALUES (1,10),(1,20),(2,5)) SELECT g, x, sum(x) OVER w, avg(x) OVER w FROM v WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY g) ORDER BY g,x;

name: WINDOW_INHERIT_FROM_BASE
description: WINDOW w2 AS (w ORDER BY ...) inherits PARTITION BY from base window
stdin: WITH v(g,x) AS (VALUES (1,10),(1,20),(2,5)) SELECT g, x, row_number() OVER w2 FROM v WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY g), w2 AS (w ORDER BY x DESC) ORDER BY g,x;

name: FETCH_FIRST_N_ROWS_ONLY
description: FETCH FIRST N ROWS ONLY is the SQL-standard equivalent of LIMIT N
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS ONLY;

name: FETCH_NEXT_N_ROWS_ONLY
description: FETCH NEXT N ROWS ONLY is interchangeable with FETCH FIRST
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x FETCH NEXT 3 ROWS ONLY;

name: OFFSET_ROWS_FETCH_NEXT
description: OFFSET N ROWS combined with FETCH NEXT M ROWS ONLY paginates
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY;

name: FETCH_FIRST_ROW_ONLY_SINGULAR
description: FETCH FIRST ROW ONLY (no count, singular ROW) returns one row
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x FETCH FIRST ROW ONLY;

name: GROUPING_SETS_BASIC
description: GROUPING SETS produces a union of subtotals
stdin: WITH v(a,b,n) AS (VALUES ('x','p',1),('x','q',2),('y','p',3)) SELECT a,b,sum(n) FROM v GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((a,b),(a),()) ORDER BY a NULLS LAST, b NULLS LAST;

name: ROLLUP_HIERARCHICAL
description: ROLLUP yields the hierarchical superset of GROUP BY plus subtotals up to grand total
stdin: WITH v(a,b,n) AS (VALUES ('x','p',1),('x','q',2),('y','p',3)) SELECT a,b,sum(n) FROM v GROUP BY ROLLUP (a,b) ORDER BY a NULLS LAST, b NULLS LAST;

name: CUBE_ALL_COMBINATIONS
description: CUBE produces all combinations of grouping columns including grand total
stdin: WITH v(a,b,n) AS (VALUES ('x','p',1),('x','q',2),('y','p',3)) SELECT a,b,sum(n) FROM v GROUP BY CUBE (a,b) ORDER BY a NULLS LAST, b NULLS LAST;

name: GROUPING_FUNCTION
description: GROUPING(col) returns 1 when col was rolled up (NULL summary) and 0 otherwise
stdin: WITH v(a,b,n) AS (VALUES ('x','p',1),('x','q',2),('y','p',3)) SELECT a, b, sum(n), GROUPING(a), GROUPING(b) FROM v GROUP BY ROLLUP (a,b) ORDER BY GROUPING(a), GROUPING(b), a, b;

name: FILTER_AGGREGATE_CLAUSE
description: agg(expr) FILTER (WHERE predicate) restricts aggregate input rows
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)) SELECT sum(x) FILTER (WHERE x % 2 = 0), count(*) FILTER (WHERE x > 2) FROM v;

name: NULLS_FIRST_ON_DESC
description: ORDER BY ... DESC NULLS FIRST overrides default DESC=NULLS FIRST behavior explicitly
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(NULL),(2),(NULL),(3)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x DESC NULLS FIRST;

name: NULLS_LAST_ON_ASC
description: ORDER BY ... ASC NULLS LAST forces NULLs to the end of ascending sort
stdin: WITH v(x) AS (VALUES (1),(NULL),(2),(NULL),(3)) SELECT x FROM v ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST;

name: CONCAT_NULL_PROPAGATES
description: The || operator propagates NULL (NULL || 'x' yields NULL)
stdin: SELECT NULL || 'x', 'a' || NULL, NULL || NULL, concat(NULL, 'x');

name: UNNEST_WITH_ORDINALITY
description: WITH ORDINALITY adds a 1-based row number column to unnest output
stdin: SELECT val, ord FROM unnest(ARRAY['a','b','c']) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(val, ord) ORDER BY ord;

name: UNNEST_MULTIPLE_ARRAYS
description: unnest(a,b) in the FROM-list expands arrays in parallel, padding with NULL
stdin: SELECT * FROM unnest(ARRAY[1,2,3], ARRAY['x','y']) AS u(a,b) ORDER BY a;

name: ON_CONFLICT_PARTIAL_INDEX_WHERE
description: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) WHERE active DO UPDATE targets a partial unique index
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_oc_partial CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_oc_partial (id int, v text, active boolean);CREATE UNIQUE INDEX bp_oc_partial_uniq ON bp_oc_partial(id) WHERE active;INSERT INTO bp_oc_partial VALUES (1, 'old', true);
stdin: INSERT INTO bp_oc_partial VALUES (1, 'new', true) ON CONFLICT (id) WHERE active DO UPDATE SET v = excluded.v RETURNING *;

name: ON_CONFLICT_DO_NOTHING_PARTIAL
description: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with WHERE clause on partial index is a no-op when matched
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_oc_nothing CASCADE;CREATE TABLE bp_oc_nothing (id int, v text, active boolean);CREATE UNIQUE INDEX bp_oc_nothing_uniq ON bp_oc_nothing(id) WHERE active;INSERT INTO bp_oc_nothing VALUES (1, 'keep', true);
stdin:
INSERT INTO bp_oc_nothing VALUES (1, 'skip', true) ON CONFLICT (id) WHERE active DO NOTHING;
SELECT * FROM bp_oc_nothing ORDER BY id;

name: GENERATED_ALWAYS_IDENTITY
description: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY assigns sequential values on INSERT
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_idgen_a CASCADE; CREATE TABLE bp_idgen_a (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, v text);
stdin: INSERT INTO bp_idgen_a (v) VALUES ('x'),('y'),('z') RETURNING *;

name: GENERATED_ALWAYS_REJECTS_EXPLICIT
description: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY rejects user-provided values without OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE
setup_stdin: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bp_idgen_areject CASCADE; CREATE TABLE bp_idgen_areject (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, v text);
stdin: INSERT INTO bp_idgen_areject (id, v) VALUES (42, 'oops');

stdin: SELECT a, b FROM bsp_btree_multi ORDER BY a, b DESC;

name: INDEX_BTREE_NULLS_FIRST
description: btree index with explicit NULLS FIRST sort property
stdin: SELECT x FROM bsp_nulls ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST;

name: BTREE_GIN_SCALAR
description: btree_gin extension enables GIN over plain scalar columns
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM bsp_btgin WHERE x = 7;

name: BTREE_GIST_SCALAR
description: btree_gist extension enables GiST over plain scalar columns
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM bsp_btgist WHERE x = 7;

name: SELECT_FOR_UPDATE_BASIC
description: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks and returns the matching rows in a single tx

name: SELECT_FOR_UPDATE_NOWAIT
description: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT succeeds when there is no contender (single-session)

name: SELECT_FOR_UPDATE_SKIP_LOCKED
description: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED returns the full row set when no rows are locked elsewhere

name: SELECT_FOR_SHARE
description: SELECT ... FOR SHARE takes a shared row lock and returns the row

name: SELECT_FOR_KEY_SHARE
description: SELECT ... FOR KEY SHARE acquires a weaker key-share lock

name: SELECT_FOR_NO_KEY_UPDATE
description: SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE allows concurrent FOR KEY SHARE

name: TXID_CURRENT_IN_TX
description: txid_current() returns a positive integer inside a transaction

name: PG_CURRENT_XACT_ID
description: pg_current_xact_id() returns the PG13+ xid8-typed transaction id

name: PG_BACKEND_PID_STABLE
description: pg_backend_pid() is stable within a session and equals itself
stdin: SELECT pg_backend_pid() = pg_backend_pid(), pg_backend_pid() > 0;

name: PG_LOCKS_CATALOG_QUERY
description: pg_locks view is queryable and returns a nonnegative row count
stdin: SELECT count(*) >= 0 FROM pg_locks;

name: ADVISORY_LOCK_AND_UNLOCK
description: pg_advisory_lock(N) and pg_advisory_unlock(N) round-trip on a single session
stdin:
SELECT pg_advisory_lock(987001) IS NULL;
SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(987001);

name: ADVISORY_TRY_LOCK
description: pg_try_advisory_lock(N) returns true when uncontended and unlock succeeds
stdin:
SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(987002);
SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(987002);

name: LOCK_TABLE_ACCESS_EXCLUSIVE
description: LOCK TABLE ... IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE succeeds in a single tx with no contender
setup_stdin:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bm_lk;
CREATE TABLE bm_lk(id int);

name: SAVEPOINT_WITH_FOR_UPDATE
description: BEGIN; SAVEPOINT; SELECT FOR UPDATE; RELEASE; COMMIT; round-trips cleanly

name: SET_TRANSACTION_ISOLATION_LEVELS
description: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL is honored across SERIALIZABLE / REPEATABLE READ / READ COMMITTED

name: SHOW_WAL_LEVEL
description: SHOW wal_level returns the configured WAL level (replica on this cluster)
stdin: SHOW wal_level;

name: PG_WAL_LSN_DIFF_SELF
description: pg_wal_lsn_diff(current, current) is 0 — useful as a deterministic shape check
stdin: SELECT pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), pg_current_wal_lsn());

name: PG_CURRENT_WAL_LSN_NONEMPTY
description: pg_current_wal_lsn() renders to a nonempty string (value is nondeterministic — shape only)
stdin: SELECT length(pg_current_wal_lsn()::text) > 0;

name: LOGICAL_SLOT_REJECTS_WAL_LEVEL_REPLICA
description: pg_create_logical_replication_slot rejects slot creation when wal_level < logical
stdin: SELECT pg_create_logical_replication_slot('beyond_slot_x', 'pgoutput');

name: PG_DROP_SLOT_IDEMPOTENT
description: Idempotent slot drop via conditional SELECT over pg_replication_slots
stdin:
SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot(slot_name) FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name = 'no_such_slot_for_beyond';
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name = 'no_such_slot_for_beyond';

name: PG_REPLICATION_SLOTS_CATALOG
description: pg_replication_slots view is queryable and returns a nonnegative count
stdin: SELECT count(*) >= 0 FROM pg_replication_slots;

name: PG_STAT_REPLICATION_NO_REPLICA
description: pg_stat_replication returns zero rows when there are no replicas
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_replication;

name: SHOW_SESSION_REPLICATION_ROLE
description: SHOW session_replication_role returns the session-default role ('origin')
stdin: SHOW session_replication_role;

name: PG_EXPORT_SNAPSHOT_SHAPE
description: pg_export_snapshot() returns a nonempty string identifier (value is nondeterministic)

name: PG_PUBLICATION_CATALOG_QUERY
description: pg_publication catalog view parses and returns a nonnegative count
stdin: SELECT count(*) >= 0 FROM pg_publication;

name: CREATE_PUBLICATION_FOR_ALL_TABLES
description: CREATE PUBLICATION FOR ALL TABLES round-trips with idempotent drop
setup_stdin: DROP PUBLICATION IF EXISTS beyond_pub_all;

name: PG_SUBSCRIPTION_CATALOG_PARSES
description: pg_subscription catalog view parses (zero rows with no actual subscription)
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_subscription;

name: PG_PUBLICATION_TABLES_VIEW
description: pg_publication_tables view parses and returns a nonnegative count
stdin: SELECT count(*) >= 0 FROM pg_publication_tables;

name: PG_STAT_WAL_RECEIVER_NO_RECEIVER
description: pg_stat_wal_receiver view returns 0 rows when not acting as a standby
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_wal_receiver;

name: LOGICAL_SLOT_PEEK_REQUIRES_SLOT
description: pg_logical_slot_peek_changes errors when slot does not exist
stdin: SELECT * FROM pg_logical_slot_peek_changes('no_such_slot', NULL, NULL);

name: LISTEN_BASIC
description: LISTEN registers a channel; pg_listening_channels() lists it; UNLISTEN clears it

name: NOTIFY_NO_PAYLOAD
description: NOTIFY without payload is accepted (no listener so no async print)
stdin:
NOTIFY beyond_no_listener;
SELECT 1;

name: NOTIFY_WITH_PAYLOAD
description: NOTIFY channel, 'payload' parses and runs
stdin:
NOTIFY beyond_no_listener, 'hello';
SELECT 1;

name: UNLISTEN_SPECIFIC
description: UNLISTEN channel removes only that channel from listening set

name: UNLISTEN_STAR_ALL
description: UNLISTEN * removes every channel from the listening set

name: PG_NOTIFY_FUNCTION_FORM
description: pg_notify('channel','payload') is the function-call form of NOTIFY
stdin: SELECT pg_notify('beyond_no_listener', 'fn-payload') IS NULL;

name: PG_NOTIFICATION_QUEUE_USAGE
description: pg_notification_queue_usage() returns a fraction in [0,1]
stdin: SELECT pg_notification_queue_usage() >= 0::float AND pg_notification_queue_usage() <= 1::float;

name: LISTEN_AND_NOTIFY_ROLLBACK
description: LISTEN + NOTIFY inside BEGIN; ROLLBACK; discards both (no async output)

name: LISTEN_INVALID_CHANNEL_NAME_ALL
description: LISTEN ALL is a syntax error (ALL is not a valid identifier here, unlike UNLISTEN *)
stdin: LISTEN ALL;

name: PG_LISTENING_CHANNELS_EMPTY
description: pg_listening_channels() returns zero rows when no LISTEN is active
stdin: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT pg_listening_channels()) s;

name: PG_LISTENING_CHANNELS_MULTI
description: pg_listening_channels() enumerates all currently-LISTENed channels

name: NOTIFY_INSIDE_FUNCTION
description: pg_notify called inside a PL/pgSQL function executes cleanly
setup_stdin:
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS beyond_notif_fn();
CREATE FUNCTION beyond_notif_fn() RETURNS int AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM pg_notify('beyond_no_listener', 'from-fn'); RETURN 7; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
stdin: SELECT beyond_notif_fn();

name: NOTIFY_INSIDE_TRIGGER
description: NOTIFY via pg_notify inside an AFTER INSERT trigger fires without error
stdin:
INSERT INTO beyond_trig_t VALUES (1);
SELECT count(*) FROM beyond_trig_t;

name: NOTIFY_EMPTY_PAYLOAD
description: NOTIFY accepts an empty-string payload and pg_notify accepts ''
stdin:
NOTIFY beyond_no_listener, '';
SELECT pg_notify('beyond_no_listener', '') IS NULL;

name: NOTIFY_LONG_PAYLOAD_100
description: NOTIFY accepts a 100-character payload (well under the 8000-byte limit)
stdin:
SELECT pg_notify('beyond_no_listener', repeat('x', 100)) IS NULL;
SELECT length(repeat('x', 100));
